knowledge:
- key_parameters: predI=Number of predictive components (Integer). If NA (default for PCA), components are computed until cumulative variance exceeds 50% (up to 10). For OPLS, single response modeling requires 1 predictive component ;; orthoI=Number of orthogonal components (Integer). Set to NA or a specific number for OPLS ;; algoC=Algorithm character (e.g., NIPALS can be selected, default is SVD if no missing values) ;; permI=Number of permutations for permutation testing (default is 20; can be increased to e.g., 1000 for rigorous p-value estimation) ;; subset=Subset of samples to use for training (e.g., "odd" or specific indices) ;; typeVc=Type of plot to generate (e.g., "x-score", "permutation") ;; parAsColFcVn=Factor or vector to color samples in plots ;; parLabVc=Labels for plotting ;; parPaletteVc=Color palette vector ;; fig.pdfC=Figure output control (e.g., "none" to suppress PDF generation)
- alternatives: SIMCA-P (commercial software) ;; K-OPLS (kernel-based OPLS package in R) ;; muma (single linear OPLS implementation in R) ;; phenomis (for importing/exporting data to text files)
- when_to_use: When analyzing high-dimensional, multi-collinear omics datasets (e.g., metabolomics, proteomics, transcriptomics) where the number of features often exceeds the number of samples. It is appropriate for unsupervised visualization (PCA), supervised regression/classification (PLS, OPLS), and feature selection (VIP values).
- pitfalls: Overfitting: High risk of perfect PLS-DA classification by chance when features exceed samples. Must check Q2Y significance via permutation testing (permI) ;; Unbalanced classes in PLS-DA: Unbalanced class sizes introduce bias in the decision rule, penalizing the larger class. Resampling or external procedures are recommended ;; Multiclass PLS-DA: PLS2 implementation with multiple classes suffers from unbalanced 0/1 proportions, making results indicative only; modeling each class separately is recommended ;; OPLS VIP: Classical VIP is not useful for single-response OPLS (identical across orthogonal components, univariate). Use predictive VIP (getVipVn(model)) and orthogonal VIP (getVipVn(model, orthoL = TRUE)) instead.

workflows.name: pca_analysis
workflows.intent: Perform unsupervised Principal Component Analysis for visualization and outlier detection.
input: dataMatrix.tsv (numeric matrix of samples as rows and variables as columns)
workflows.stages: 1. Run PCA using opls ;; 2. Plot default summary figures ;; 3. Customize score plots with sample metadata coloring and labels
workflows.code:
sacurine.pca <- opls(sacurine$dataMatrix)
plot(sacurine.pca)
genderFc <- sacurine$sampleMetadata[, "gender"]
plot(sacurine.pca, typeVc = "x-score", parAsColFcVn = genderFc)
plot(sacurine.pca, typeVc = "x-score", parAsColFcVn = genderFc, parLabVc = as.character(sacurine$sampleMetadata[, "age"]), parPaletteVc = c("green4", "magenta"))

workflows.name: supervised_pls_opls
workflows.intent: Perform supervised classification or regression with cross-validation, permutation testing, and performance evaluation on a test set.
input: dataMatrix.tsv (numeric matrix of samples as rows and variables as columns)
sampleMetadata.tsv (sample metadata containing the response variable)
workflows.stages: 1. Run PLS-DA or OPLS-DA using opls ;; 2. Train model on a subset of samples ;; 3. Evaluate predictions on training and test subsets ;; 4. Extract VIP values for feature selection
workflows.code:
sacurine.plsda <- opls(sacurine$dataMatrix, genderFc)
sacurine.oplsda <- opls(sacurine$dataMatrix, genderFc, predI = 1, orthoI = NA)
sacurine.oplsda <- opls(sacurine$dataMatrix, genderFc, predI = 1, orthoI = NA, subset = "odd")
trainVi <- getSubsetVi(sacurine.oplsda)
confusion_train.tb <- table(genderFc[trainVi], fitted(sacurine.oplsda))
confusion_test.tb <- table(genderFc[-trainVi], predict(sacurine.oplsda, sacurine$dataMatrix[-trainVi, ]))
vipVn <- getVipVn(opls(sacurine$dataMatrix, ageVn, predI = 1, orthoI = NA, fig.pdfC = "none"))

workflows.name: summarized_experiment_workflow
workflows.intent: Perform PLS-DA or OPLS-DA directly on a SummarizedExperiment object and extract results.
input: SummarizedExperiment object (containing assay data and colData metadata)
workflows.stages: 1. Run PLS-DA using opls on the SummarizedExperiment ;; 2. Extract the updated object with scores and loadings ;; 3. Extract and plot the model scores
workflows.code:
sac.se <- opls(sac.se, "gender")
head(SummarizedExperiment::colData(sac.se))
head(SummarizedExperiment::rowData(sac.se))
sac_opls.ls <- getOpls(sac.se)
plot(sac_opls.ls[["gender_PLSDA"]], typeVc = "x-score")
plot_score(sac.se, model.c = "gender_PLSDA", plotly.l = TRUE, info.vc = "all")

workflows.name: multi_assay_experiment_workflow
workflows.intent: Build PLS-DA models in parallel for multiple datasets within a MultiAssayExperiment.
workflows.stages: 1. Run PLS-DA using opls on the MultiAssayExperiment ;; 2. Extract individual models ;; 3. Plot scores for a specific dataset
workflows.code:
nci.mae <- opls(nci.mae, "cancer", predI = 2, fig.pdfC = "none")
SummarizedExperiment::colData(nci.mae[["agilent"]])
mae_opls.ls <- getOpls(nci.mae)
plot(mae_opls.ls[["agilent"]][["cancer_PLSDA"]], typeVc = "x-score")
